question: Who first described the nucleus as a cell organelle in 1831?
solution: The correct answer is __**Robert Brown**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** • **Robert Brown**, a prominent **Scottish botanist**, is credited with the discovery and description of the **cell nucleus** in the year **1831**. • While examining the **epidermis** of **orchids** under a **microscope**, he noticed an opaque area within the cells, which he termed the **nucleus** (derived from the Latin word for "kernel" or "nut"). • This discovery was a fundamental milestone in the field of **cytology** (cell biology), as it challenged the previous notion that the **cell wall** was the only significant part of a cell. • His observations helped scientists understand that cells have internal **organization** and specialized **organelles** responsible for various biological processes. • Brown's work paved the way for the later formulation of the **Cell Theory**, as it highlighted a consistent internal structure across different types of **plant cells**.
